Definition: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3144; something evidential, i.e. (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle):--to be testified, testimony, witness.
BiblicalUsage: martýrion is a testimony, something evidential, the proof offered. In 1 Corinthians 1:6 the testimony of Christ is confirmed in the Corinthians, and in 1 Corinthians 2:1 Paul declares the testimony of God without excellency of speech. In 1 Timothy 2:6 Christ gives Himself a ransom for all, to be testified in due time, and in 2 Corinthians 1:12 Paul's rejoicing is the testimony of his conscience, in simplicity and godly sincerity. The word is the proof that stands up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe martýrion shows me that my conscience can testify for me or against me. I hold that a clear conscience is worth more than a clever defence.
